ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Tips for Making a Habit Stick

fullPassage:
Tips for Making a Habit Stick

Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through repetition, so make the change easier to repeat. Second, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an existing one, for example, "After brushing my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes." When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of calming music while meditating. Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement and helps you keep going. Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up where you left off.

questions.passage: ①<u>Forming</u> a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. ②<u>Here</u> are five ways to start a habit that really <u>sticks</u>. ③<u>First</u>, start small. Don't try <u>④<u>doing</u></u> too much, too quickly. A habit is <u>formed</u> through repetition, so make the change <u>easier</u> to repeat.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② doing → to do. 'Don't try to do'에서 try + to부정사(~하려고 노력하다). 부정문 맥락에서 '너무 많은 것을 하려고 하지 마라'.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ② doing: try + to부정사(노력하다) vs try + -ing(시도하다). '하지 마라'는 금지 맥락에서 to do가 적절
❌ ① sticks: 관계대명사절 동사, 주어 a habit(단수). 올바름
❌ ③ formed: 수동태 is formed. 올바름
❌ ④ easier: 비교급, make + O + C 구문. 올바름
det.tip: try to do = ~하려고 노력하다(목표 지향). try doing = ~해 보다(실험적). Don't try to do = 하려고 하지 마라

questions.passage: ①<u>Second</u>, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll ②<u>③<u>meditate</u></u> regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." ④<u>This</u> works even <u>better</u> if you combine your new habit with an <u>existing</u> one. When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more <u>likely</u> to stick. Third, make it <u>attractively</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ attractively → attractive. 'make it attractive'에서 make + O + 형용사(보어). 부사 attractively는 보어 자리에 올 수 없음.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ attractively: make + it + 형용사(보어). 부사는 보어 불가
❌ ① better: 비교급, well의 비교급. 올바름
❌ ② existing: 현재분사→형용사, 명사 수식. 올바름
❌ ③ likely: be likely to = ~할 가능성이 있다. 올바름
det.tip: make + O + 형용사(보어): make it attractive(매력적으로 만들다). 부사 ≠ 보어

questions.passage: You ①<u>could</u> listen to your favorite piece of calming music <u>while</u> meditating. ②<u>Fourth</u>, track your progress. ③<u>Mark</u> a calendar with an X every time you <u>finish</u> something. <u>④<u>Seeing</u></u> the progress gives you a sense of achievement and helps you <u>keeping</u> going.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ keeping → keep. 'helps you keep going'에서 help + O + 동사원형. keeping(동명사)은 불가.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ keeping: help + O + V(원형). helps you keep going이 올바름
❌ ① while: 접속사, 분사구문과 함께. 올바름
❌ ② finish: every time절 동사. 올바름
❌ ③ Seeing: 동명사 주어. 올바름
det.tip: help + 목적어 + 동사원형/to부정사. help + O + -ing 불가. helps you keep = 계속하도록 돕다

questions.passage: ①<u>After</u> <u>brushing</u> my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes. ②<u>When</u> your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. ③<u>Pair</u> your new change with <u>that</u> you love. ④<u>Seeing</u> the progress gives you a sense of achievement. If you find <u>that</u> your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up <u>where</u> you left off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② that → what. 'Pair your new change with what you love.' 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what(~하는 것)이 필요. that은 선행사가 없으면 사용 불가.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ② that: 원문은 what(선행사 포함 관계대명사). with 뒤에 선행사가 없으므로 what 필요
❌ ① brushing: 전치사 After + 동명사. 올바름
❌ ③ that: 접속사, find의 목적절. 올바름
❌ ④ where: 관계부사, 장소. 올바름
det.tip: what = the thing(s) that. 선행사 없이 관계절 이끎. with what you love = 당신이 사랑하는 것과 함께

questions.passage: A ①<u>habit</u> is formed through <u>repetition</u>, so make the change easier to repeat. ②<u>When</u> your fixed habit becomes a <u>cue</u> for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. ③<u>Third</u>, make it attractive. <u>④<u>Pair</u></u> your new change with what you love. Fifth, be flexible. If your progress has stopped, just <u>give up</u> where you left off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ give up(포기하다) → pick up(다시 시작하다). 원문: 'just pick up where you left off.' 중단 시 다시 시작하라는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ give up: 원문은 pick up(다시 시작하다). 유연성을 강조하는 맥락에 give up(포기) 부적절
❌ ① repetition(반복): 원문 그대로
❌ ② cue(신호): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ Pair(짝짓다): 원문 그대로
det.tip: pick up(다시 시작하다) ↔ give up(포기하다). pick up where you left off = 중단한 곳에서 다시 시작

questions.passage: Don't say, "I'll ①<u>②<u>meditate</u></u> regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." ③<u>This</u> works even better if you <u>combine</u> your new habit with an existing one. ④<u>Mark</u> a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of <u>achievement</u> and helps you keep going. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has <u>accelerated</u> for any reason, just pick up where you <u>left</u> off.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ accelerated(가속된) → stopped(멈춘). 원문: 'your progress has stopped' — 진행이 멈춘 경우 다시 시작하라는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ③ accelerated: 원문은 stopped(멈춘). 진행이 멈춘 상황에서 다시 시작하라는 조언
❌ ① combine(결합하다): 원문 그대로
❌ ② achievement(성취): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ left(떠난): 원문 그대로 (left off = 중단한)
det.tip: stopped(멈춘) ↔ accelerated(가속된). progress has stopped = 진행이 중단된

questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"새로운 습관을 형성하는 것은 처음부터 쉽다."

det.korean: 원문: 'Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning.' — 쉽지 않다고 했으므로 F.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 원문은 not easy(쉽지 않다). '쉽다'는 원문과 반대
❌ T: 원문과 불일치
det.tip: not easy = 쉽지 않다. especially in the beginning = 특히 처음에는

questions.passage: Second, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an existing one, for example, "After brushing my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes."
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"새 습관을 기존 습관과 결합하면 더 효과적이다."

det.korean: 원문: 'This works even better if you combine your new habit with an existing one.' — 결합하면 더 효과적. T.
det.analysis:
✅ T: 원문 'works even better if you combine' 일치
❌ F: 원문과 일치하므로 부적절
det.tip: combine A with B = A를 B와 결합하다. works even better = 훨씬 더 잘 작동한다

questions.passage: Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement and helps you keep going.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"달력에 X 표시를 하면 좌절감을 느끼게 된다."

det.korean: 원문: 'Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement' — 성취감을 준다고 했지 좌절감이 아님. F.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 원문은 a sense of achievement(성취감). 좌절감은 원문과 반대
❌ T: 원문과 불일치
det.tip: achievement(성취) ≠ frustration(좌절). 진행 확인 → 성취감 → 지속 동기

questions.passage:
Tips for Making a Habit Stick

Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through repetition, so make the change easier to repeat. Second, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an existing one, for example, "After brushing my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes." When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 두 번째 조언(목표를 구체적으로 설정하라)의 핵심 원리는?
ch: 최대한 많은 습관을 동시에 시작해야 한다
명상은 매일 한 시간씩 해야 효과가 있다
구체적 목표와 기존 습관 연결이 새 습관 정착을 돕는다
기존 습관을 모두 버리고 새로 시작해야 한다

det.korean: 구체적 목표 설정(specific) + 기존 습관과 결합(combine) → 고정 습관이 신호(cue)가 되어 정착.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 구체적 목표+기존 습관 연결: 원문의 specific + combine + cue 논리 요약
❌ ① 많은 습관 동시: 원문은 start small
❌ ② 한 시간: five minutes each day
❌ ③ 기존 습관 버리기: combine with existing one과 반대
det.tip: 핵심 논리: specific goal → combine with existing → cue for action → habit sticks

questions.passage: Third, make it attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of calming music while meditating. Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement and helps you keep going. Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up where you left off.
questions.stem: 세 번째~다섯 번째 조언을 관통하는 공통 원리로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 완벽하지 않으면 처음부터 다시 시작해야 한다
긍정적 감정과 유연한 태도가 습관 지속의 핵심이다

det.korean: 3번째(매력적으로), 4번째(성취감), 5번째(유연하게) → 모두 긍정적 감정 + 유연한 태도가 핵심.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 긍정적 감정+유연한 태도: attractive(매력), achievement(성취), flexible(유연) 관통
❌ ① 고통+인내: 원문은 즐겁게 하라는 조언
❌ ③ 타인의 감시: 언급 없음
❌ ④ 처음부터 다시: pick up where you left off(중단점에서 재개)
det.tip: 3~5번 조언 공통: 즐기기(attractive) + 성취감(achievement) + 유연성(flexible)

questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Don't try to do too much, too quickly. A habit is formed through repetition, so make the change easier to repeat. Second, make your goal specific. Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day."
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 새로운 습관은 처음부터 크게 시작해야 한다
매일 한 시간씩 명상해야 효과가 있다

det.korean: 원문: 'A habit is formed through repetition' — 습관은 반복을 통해 형성.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 반복을 통해 형성: 원문 그대로
❌ ① 크게 시작: start small(작게 시작)과 반대
❌ ② 막연하게: specific(구체적으로)과 반대
❌ ④ 한 시간: five minutes(5분)
det.tip: formed through repetition = 반복을 통해 형성됨. start small = 작게 시작

questions.passage: Third, make it attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of calming music while meditating. Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up where you left off.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 좋아하는 차분한 음악을 들으며 명상할 수 있다
진행이 멈추면 즉시 포기하는 것이 좋다

det.korean: 원문: 'just pick up where you left off' — 중단 시 다시 시작하라. ①의 '즉시 포기'는 원문과 반대.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ① 즉시 포기: 원문은 pick up(다시 시작). 포기가 아니라 재개
❌ ② 차분한 음악: calming music 일치
❌ ③ 달력 표시: Mark a calendar with an X 일치
❌ ④ 시간 걸림: takes time 일치
det.tip: pick up where you left off = 중단한 곳에서 다시 시작 ≠ 포기

questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Second, make your goal specific. Third, make it attractive. Fourth, track your progress. Fifth, be flexible.
questions.stem: 다음 중 위 글의 내용에 비추어 틀린 문장은?
ch: The article suggests starting with small changes rather than big ones.
The article advises being strict and never missing a day of your new habit.
Setting specific goals is one of the five tips for making a habit stick.
Tracking progress helps maintain motivation for the new habit.

det.korean: ③ 원문은 'be flexible'(유연하라). strict(엄격하게) + never missing(절대 빠지지 마라)는 원문과 반대.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ③ strict/never missing: 원문은 flexible + pick up where you left off. 빠져도 다시 시작하라
❌ ① small changes: start small 일치
❌ ② specific goals: make your goal specific 일치
❌ ④ tracking motivation: track progress → achievement → keep going 일치
det.tip: flexible(유연한) ↔ strict(엄격한). 핵심: 빠져도 괜찮다, 다시 시작하면 된다

questions.passage: Don't say, "I'll meditate regularly." Say, "I'll meditate for five minutes each day." This works even better if you combine your new habit with an existing one, for example, "After brushing my teeth in the morning, I'll meditate for five minutes." When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. You could listen to your favorite piece of calming music while meditating. Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement and helps you keep going. Fifth, be flexible.
questions.stem: 본문에서 찾아 다음 말을 찾아 쓰시오. "고정된 습관이 행동의 __________가 되면, 새 습관은 정착될 가능성이 높아진다." (**영어** 단어를 쓰시오) (조건: 1단어 사용) (1단어)

det.korean: 원문: 'a cue for action' — 행동의 신호.
det.analysis: ✅ cue: 원문에서 직접 찾기. 행동을 유발하는 신호/단서
det.tip: cue(신호/단서). 행동 유발 trigger. habit loop: cue → routine → reward

questions.passage: Fourth, track your progress. Mark a calendar with an X every time you finish something. Seeing the progress gives you __________ and helps you keep going. (achieve → 명사형)
questions.stem:
다음 빈칸에 주어진 단어를 올바른 형태로 바꿔 완성하시오.

(achieve를 적절한 명사형으로 바꿀 것) (조건: 4단어 사용) (4단어)

det.korean: 원문: 'gives you a sense of achievement' — 성취감을 준다.
det.analysis: ✅ a sense of achievement: 원문에서 직접 찾기. 달력 표시를 통한 진행 확인 → 성취감
det.tip: a sense of achievement = 성취감. sense of + 명사: ~감, ~의식

questions.passage: Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, __________.

[just / where / pick / you / off / left / up]

(모든 단어를 사용할 것, 대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능) (조건: 7단어 사용) (7단어)

det.tip: pick up where you left off = 중단한 곳에서 다시 시작하다. 관용 표현 암기 필수

questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. Second, make your goal specific. Third, make it attractive. Fourth, track your progress. Fifth, be flexible. Forming a new habit takes time.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 학교 공부를 잘하기 위한 시간 관리 기술
새로운 습관을 효과적으로 정착시키는 다섯 가지 방법

det.korean: 글 전체가 습관 정착을 위한 5가지 방법(small, specific, attractive, track, flexible)을 제시.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 다섯 가지 방법: 글의 구조 그대로 (First~Fifth)
❌ ② 명상: 예시일 뿐 주제가 아님
❌ ③ 시간 관리: 언급 없음
❌ ④ 운동: 언급 없음
det.tip: 주제문: 'five ways to start a habit that really sticks'

questions.passage: When your fixed habit becomes a cue for action, your new habit is more likely to stick. Third, make it attractive. Pair your new change with what you love. Fourth, track your progress. Seeing the progress gives you a sense of achievement. Fifth, be flexible. If you find that your progress has stopped for any reason, just pick up where you left off.
questions.stem:
위 글을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

"By making habits __________, tracking progress, and staying flexible, you can make new habits stick."
ch: enjoyable and connected to existing routines

det.korean: 습관을 즐겁고 기존 루틴과 연결하면(attractive + combine with existing) 정착 가능.
det.analysis:
✅ ② enjoyable + connected to existing: attractive(매력적) + combine(기존과 연결)
❌ ① difficult/painful: 원문 반대
❌ ③ isolated: combine과 반대
❌ ④ strict/unchangeable: flexible과 반대
det.tip: 핵심 키워드: attractive(매력적) + combine(연결) + track(추적) + flexible(유연)

questions.passage: Forming a new habit is not easy, especially in the beginning. Here are five ways to start a habit that really sticks. First, start small. A habit is created through repetition, so make the change easier to repeat.
questions.stem:
다음 한국어 문장을 주어진 조건에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오.

"습관은 반복을 통해 형성된다."

→ A habit is __________ through repetition.

(한 단어, 수동태 형태로 쓰시오) (조건: 1단어 사용) (1단어)

det.korean: 원문: 'A habit is formed through repetition.' — 수동태. 형성되다.
det.analysis: ✅ formed: be + p.p. 수동태. form(형성하다) → is formed(형성되다)
det.tip: form(동사: 형성하다) → formed(과거분사). 수동태: is formed = 형성되다
